expectation: Membrane/cytoplasmic ring on a subset of CD68+/IBA1+ macrophages, uncommon, scattered single cells or small clusters in lamina propria, stroma and around vessels; epithelium and background should be negative.
observed: A: many small bright yellow specks scattered through stroma, some in epithelium and edges, with no obvious pattern. B: one saturated blob plus a few ring-shaped cells at top. C: lone speck. D: irregular saturated blob, debris-like. E1: faint membrane rings in a cluster whose shape matches the IBA1+ cells; E3 shows partial white overlap.
why: Most bright spots look like speckle or debris, but E shows low-contrast membrane rings on IBA1+ macrophage clusters, as the marker graph predicts.
notes: Bright specks in A, C and D look like debris and should not drive the verdict. In the IBA1-dense field (E) CD163 outlines a subset of IBA1+ cells as membrane rings, so a real but low-contrast stain.
